title: Bea 'sy valley beg
description: Ten short stories about life in small Manx villages: a baker with grainy bread and cinnamon buns, a farm that makes cheese by a river, an atheist buried in the churchyard, a village doctor's winter diary, a grandmother's tale of a wolf and a barberry hedge, a letter about an uncle's will and his heraldic sign, an art gallery in an old chapel, a radio talk show about a new road, a garden ready for the village show, and a band that practises in old wartime barracks.

lessons.title: Yn shapp arran 'sy valley
lessons.summary: Tanguy Jaouen bakes grainy bread from island wheat in a small village near Ramsey; he keeps his yeast cold and mixes it with a litre of warm water each evening, makes cinnamon buns with citrus peel on Saturdays, and an American visitor, Maela Quinlan, who has only dollars, buys a box of buns and leaves a dollar note to hang on his wall.
lessons.text:
Ta Tanguy Jaouen jannoo arran ayns balley beg faggys da Rhumsaa. Ta'n shapp arran echey er y straid vooar, eddyr yn agglish as y thie-oast. T'eh girree ec kiare er y chlag dagh moghrey, as ta'n chied arran aarloo roish shey. She shapp beg eh, agh t'eh saiagh son y valley. Ta sleih y valley kionnaghey arran çheh er nyn raad dys yn obbyr.

Ta Tanguy jannoo e arran lesh curnaght veih ny magheryn ayns yiass yn ellan. Cha nel eh jannoo yn curnaght ro veen: t'eh freayll ayrnyn beggey jeh'n grine ayn. Er-y-fa shen, ta'n arran echey grineagh. Ta ny paitçhyn 'sy valley gra dy vel arran grineagh ro chreoi, agh s'mie lesh ny shenn sleih eh. “Ta arran grineagh mie son y chorp,” ta Tanguy gra. “Ta arran bog ny shappyn mooarey saiagh son keeagh, agh cha nel eh saiagh son deiney.”

Cha nel arran erbee gyn jastee. Ta Tanguy freayll y jastee echey ayns kishtey feayr, son dy vel jastee goll marroo ayns çhiass. Dagh fastyr, t'eh cur jastee ayns leetyr dy ushtey çheh, as t'eh lhiggey da'n jastee gobbraghey rish oor. Eisht t'eh cur yn ushtey shen er y curnaght, marish sollan as leetyr elley dy ushtey. Ta'n arran gaase 'syn oie.

Dagh Jesarn, ta Tanguy jannoo arran millish lesh cannial. T'eh cur crackan messyn kidragh ayns yn arran millish neesht: crackan oranje, myr sampleyr. Ta blass ny messyn kidragh as y cannial cooidjagh feer vie, as ta'n arran millish ooilley creckit roish nuy.

Un Jesarn, haink ben noa stiagh 'sy shapp. She Maela Quinlan v'ee, turrysagh veih America. “Ta mee laccal shey jeh ny arranyn cannial,” dooyrt ee, “agh cha nel agh dollaryn aym. Vel shiu goaill dollaryn?”

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Tanguy. “Cha nel mee er vakin dollar rieau 'sy shapp shoh.” Agh va Maela jeeaghyn trimshagh. Hug Tanguy shey arranyn cannial ayns bocs pabyr. “Gow yn bocs,” dooyrt eh. “Eeck mee laa elley, my vees punt ayd.”

Haink Maela er-ash 'sy fastyr cheddin, lesh punt son y bocs, as lesh dollar neesht. “Son y voalley,” dooyrt ee. Nish ta'n dollar shen croghey er boalley y shapp. Ta Tanguy gra rish dy chooilley turrysagh: “Va'n chied dollar dy bragh 'sy shapp shoh son bocs dy arran cannial.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta'n arran echey grineagh?
Ta'n arran grineagh, son dy vel Tanguy freayll ayrnyn beggey jeh'n grine ayn.
Cre ta Tanguy jannoo lesh y jastee dagh fastyr?
T'eh cur jastee ayns leetyr dy ushtey çheh, as t'eh lhiggey da gobbraghey rish oor.
Cre ta Tanguy cur ayns yn arran millish marish y cannial?
T'eh cur crackan messyn kidragh ayn: crackan oranje, myr sampleyr.
Cre hug Tanguy da Maela?
Hug eh shey arranyn cannial ayns bocs pabyr.
Cre ta croghey er boalley y shapp nish?
Ta dollar croghey er boalley y shapp.

lessons.title: Caashey ec y thalloo
lessons.summary: Eurig Hendra keeps cows on a farm by a river: the alluvial fields below give good grass, the marsh above grows only purple moor grass; he and his daughter Llio curdle the milk and wrap the young cheeses in straw, a blackbird sings on the barn, a clod of earth sticks to her boot, barley awns scratch her arms, and her hat is caught in an eddy in the river.
lessons.text:
Ta Eurig Hendra cummal er thalloo beg rish awin, mean-raad eddyr daa valley. Ta kiare as feed booa echey, as t'eh jannoo caashey jeh'n bainney oc. Ta e inneen Llio, kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash, gobbraghey marish e ayr ec y jerrey-shiaghtin.

Ta daa ayrn er y thalloo. Rish yn awin, ta ny magheryn injil as rea. She thalloo gleayragh t'ayn: haink y thalloo shen sheese lesh yn awin. Ta thalloo gleayragh feer vie son faiyr, as ta ny baa gee ayns shen 'sy tourey. Erskyn ny magheryn shen, ta boglagh mooar. Ta'n boglagh fliugh car ny bleeaney, as cha nel agh brabbanagh gaase ayn. Ta'n brabbanagh aalin ayns Mean Fouyir, glass as gorrym, agh cha nel ny baa laccal ee y ee. “Cha nel ymmyd ayns y boglagh,” ta Eurig gra, “agh ta ny ushagyn feer ghennal ayn.”

Dagh moghrey Jesarn, ta Eurig as Llio jannoo caashey. T'ad cur y bainney ayns saagh mooar, as t'ad cur stoo er lheh ayn, as ta'n bainney glubbey. “Jeeagh,” ta Eurig gra, “ta'n bainney glubbey nish. Ta'n ayrn chreoi scarrey veih'n ushtey.” Lurg oor, ta'n bainney glubbey dy slane, as t'ad cur yn ayrn chreoi ayns cummaghyn. “Mannagh vel y bainney glubbey,” ta Eurig gra, “cha bee caashey ayn.”

Ta Eurig freayll y caashey aeg ayns coonlagh. T'eh cur coonlagh glen mygeayrt dagh caashey, as t'eh kiangley y coonlagh lesh tead. Ta'n coonlagh freayll y caashey çhirrym as feayr. Ta ny caashaghyn lhie ayns y thie-stoyr rish shey meeghyn.

Ta lhondoo cummal er mullagh y thie-stoyr. Dagh moghrey t'eh goaill arrane er y mullagh: ushag doo lesh gob buigh. “Ta'n lhondoo shen goaill arrane ny share na mish,” ta Eurig gra, as ta Llio gearey.

Lurg y caashey, ta Llio goll dys y vagher. Ta thalloo fliugh ec y yiat, as ta croaglagh mooar dy halloo lhiantyn rish e braag. T'ee bwoalley yn croaglagh jeh'n vraag er clagh, agh ta croaglagh elley lhiantyn rish y vraag elley. Eisht t'ee gymmyrkey oarn er son ny baa. Ta caulgyn liauyr er yn oarn, as ta ny caulgyn cur pian er e laueyn. “Ta ram caulgyn er yn oarn shoh,” t'ee gra.

'Sy fastyr, ta Llio soie rish yn awin. Ta'n gheay goaill e edd, as ta'n edd tuittym 'syn ushtey. Ta eeirey 'syn awin: ta'n ushtey cassey mygeayrt as mygeayrt. Ta'n edd cassey 'syn eeirey, reesht as reesht. Lesh banglane liauyr, ta Llio tayrn yn edd magh ass yn eeirey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta'n thalloo rish yn awin feer vie son faiyr?
She thalloo gleayragh t'ayn, as ta thalloo gleayragh feer vie son faiyr.
Cre ta gaase ayns y boglagh?
Cha nel agh brabbanagh gaase ayns y boglagh.
Cre ta Eurig cur mygeayrt dagh caashey?
T'eh cur coonlagh glen mygeayrt dagh caashey.
C'raad ta'n lhondoo cummal?
Ta'n lhondoo cummal er mullagh y thie-stoyr.
Cre ta ny caulgyn jannoo?
Ta ny caulgyn cur pian er laueyn Llio.
Cre haink er edd Llio?
Huitt yn edd 'syn ushtey, as v'eh cassey 'syn eeirey, derrey ren Llio tayrn eh magh lesh banglane.

lessons.title: Yn oanluckey 'sy ruillick
lessons.summary: Caoimhe Jacka's grandfather, an atheist all his life, asked to be buried beside his wife in the village churchyard; the vicar Garmon Trewhella agrees and makes a short liturgy, shows her the carved frieze of village figures over the door, tells her how the villagers once paid a tithe, and they remember that the old man gave alms to the poor every winter in spite of his disbelief.
lessons.text:
Hooar shenn-ayr Caoimhe Jacka baase 'sy gheurey, tra v'eh nuy bleeaney as feed as three feed d'eash. V'eh ny eirinagh 'sy valley rish e vea ooilley. Cha row eh rieau 'syn agglish, agh ec poosaghyn as ec baaseyn. Va anjeeys echey: cha row eh credjal ayns Jee erbee. “Cha nel flaunys ayn,” v'eh gra, “agh ta'n seihll shoh aalin dy liooar.”

Agh roish e vaase, dooyrt eh rish Caoimhe: “Ta mee laccal dy bee mee er my oanluckey ayns y ruillick 'sy valley, rish my ven.” Va e ven er ny oanluckey ayns shen roish jeih bleeaney.

Hie Caoimhe dys y saggyrt, Garmon Trewhella. “Va anjeeys ec my henn-ayr,” dooyrt ee. “Jean oo eh y oanluckey 'sy ruillick, ga dy row meechredjue echey?”

“Nee,” dooyrt Garmon. “Ta ynnyd ayns y ruillick son dy chooilley pheiagh 'sy valley. Cha nel meechredjue ny resoon dy lhiettal dooinney veih e ven. Ver mee liturgey giare: arrane as padjer as fockle mychione e vea.” Va Caoimhe feer ghennal. Cha row ee laccal liturgey liauyr, as cha beagh e shenn-ayr er laccal eh.

Ren Garmon soilshaghey yn agglish da Caoimhe. Erskyn y dorrys, va freesh liauyr jeh clagh. Ayns y freesh va cummeydaneyn beggey giarit: eirinee lesh kirree, eeasteyryn lesh lieen, mraane lesh arran. “Va'n freesh shoh giarit roish queig cheead bleeaney,” dooyrt Garmon. “Ta ny cummeydaneyn sleih y valley, as cha nel fys ec peiagh erbee er nyn enmyn.”

“Ayns ny laghyn shen,” dooyrt Garmon, “va dy chooilley eirinagh eeck jaghee da'n agglish: un ayrn jeh jeih jeh'n arroo echey. Cha row yn jaghee mie lesh ny eirinee boghtey, as va ram streeu mychione y jaghee.” Ren Caoimhe gearey. “V'eh gra dy beagh eh er obbal yn jaghee,” dooyrt ee. “Va meechredjue echey ayns jaghee as ayns flaunys cooidjagh.”

“Agh ta fys aym er red elley mychione dty henn-ayr,” dooyrt Garmon. “Dagh geurey, haink eh dys y thie aym lesh argid as lesh ooylyn. ‘Son ny boghtyn,’ v'eh gra. Va'n jeirk echey ny smoo na'n jeirk ec sleih erbee elley 'sy valley. Agh cha by laccal lesh dy beagh fys ec sleih er.”

Cha row fys ec Caoimhe er y jeirk, as ren ee keayney.

Va'n oanluckey er laa feayr, glen. Ren Garmon y liturgey giare, as hie yn shenn dooinney fo'n thalloo rish e ven. Lurg y liturgey, dooyrt Caoimhe rish Garmon: “Cha nel fys aym vel flaunys ayn ny dyn.”

“As cha nel fys aym's dy firrinagh,” dooyrt Garmon, “agh ta fys aym dy row eh dooinney mie.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh row shenn-ayr Caoimhe 'syn agglish dy mennick?
Va anjeeys echey: cha row eh credjal ayns Jee erbee.
C'raad va'n shenn dooinney laccal ve er ny oanluckey?
V'eh laccal ve er ny oanluckey ayns y ruillick 'sy valley, rish e ven.
Cre ta ry-akin 'sy freesh erskyn y dorrys?
Ta cummeydaneyn beggey ayn: eirinee, eeasteyryn as mraane lesh arran.
Cre dooyrt Caoimhe mychione flaunys lurg y liturgey?
Dooyrt ee nagh vel fys eck vel flaunys ayn ny dyn.
Cre va'n shenn dooinney cur da ny boghtyn dagh geurey?
V'eh cur jeirk daue: argid as ooylyn.

lessons.title: Lioar-laa yn lhee
lessons.summary: In his diary the village doctor Ieuan Penna describes one winter Monday: half the village has flu, a fisherman's cut has become infected, a woman's dizziness comes from an infection behind her eardrum and not from her cerebellum, a boy has a bee sting near his eyelid, and Tegen Polmear's baby has swollen eyelids, a common thing in infancy.
lessons.text:
Lioar-laa Ieuan Penna. Jelune, Jerrey Geuree.

Ta mee er ve my lhee 'sy valley shoh rish queig bleeaney yeig, as cha vaik mee rieau geurey gollrish y geurey shoh. Ta'n floo ec lieh ny sleih. Haink ram sleih dys y thie-lheihys jiu, nuy jeig jeu, as va'n floo ec shiaght jeu. Ta'n floo cur er sleih ve lag as çheh, as t'ad ching rish shiaghtin ny ny smoo. Ta mee gra rish dy chooilley pheiagh lesh floo: “Immee thie, gow ushtey, as fuirree 'sy lhiabbee.” Cha nel lheihys erbee ny share na shen.

Haink eeasteyr aeg stiagh 'sy voghrey. V'eh er ghiarey e laue lesh skynn roish tree laghyn. Va'n beam beg, agh cha row eh er ghlenney yn beam. Jiu va'n laue echey ruy as trome, as va'n beam doghanit. Ren mee glenney yn beam, as hug mee lheihys da. “Tra t'ou giarey dty laue,” dooyrt mee, “glen yn beam dy chooilley cheayrt. Ta beam doghanit feer ghaueagh.”

Lurg shen, haink shenn ven as dullyraght urree. Va'n dullyraght urree rish daa laa: va'n thie cassey mygeayrt urree tra ren ee girree. V'ee ayns aggle dy row red ennagh neuchadjin ayns e kione. “Ta'n kerebellum reaghey y chorp tra t'ou shassoo as shooyl,” dooyrt mee rish y ven. “Foddee dullyraght çheet ass y kerebellum, agh ta dullyraght çheet ass y chleaysh ny smoo dy mennick.” Ren mee jeeaghyn 'sy chleaysh eck. Va'n dollan cleayshey ruy, as va ushtey doghanit cooyl y dollan. Cha row eh y kerebellum, agh y chleaysh. Hug mee lheihys jee, as v'ee feer ghennal.

Fastyr, haink guilley beg lesh e voir. V'eh er ve cloie 'sy gharey, as va guin shellan er, faggys da e hooill. Va'n farvollee echey mooar as ruy, as cha row eh abyl foshley e hooill. Hug mee lheihys feayr er y guin. “Bee y farvollee mie lurg laa ny ghaa,” dooyrt mee, “agh my vees guin elley ort, tar hym reesht.”

Er y jerrey, haink Tegen Polmear lesh e lhiannoo, kiare meeghyn d'eash. Va farvollee yn lhiannoo mooar as ruy neesht, as va Tegen ayns aggle. Ta red shoh feer chadjin ayns lambaanys: ta sooillyn ny paitçhyn aegey beg as moal. “Ayns lambaanys,” dooyrt mee rish Tegen, “ta ram doghanyn beggey çheet as goll. Glen ny farvollee lesh ushtey çheh, as bee ad mie.”

Va laa liauyr aym. Cha nel ec y lhee laa erbee gyn obbyr 'sy gheurey, agh ta mee gennal dy vel y valley shoh aym.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n çhingys va ec ram sleih 'sy valley?
Va'n floo ec lieh ny sleih.
Cre'n fa va'n beam ec yn eeasteyr doghanit?
Cha row eh er ghlenney yn beam lurg da ghiarey e laue.
Cre'n fa va dullyraght er y shenn ven?
Va ushtey doghanit cooyl y dollan cleayshey eck.
Cre haink er y guilley beg 'sy gharey?
Va guin shellan er, as va'n farvollee echey mooar as ruy.
Cre ta feer chadjin ayns lambaanys?
Ta farvollee mooar as doghanyn beggey feer chadjin ayns lambaanys.

lessons.title: Yn filliu as y barbrag
lessons.summary: Riwal pricks his hands on barberry thorns while picking berries, and his grandmother Soazig Kervella tells him the village superstition that the barberry by the gate must never be cut, and the old tale of a wolf mad with hunger that was kept out of the village by a girl's magic hedge of barberry and periwinkle; Riwal calls it superstition, like the astrology in her paper, and she laughs.
lessons.text:
Ta Riwal jeih bleeaney d'eash. Ta e shenn-voir, Soazig Kervella, cummal ayns thie beg ec jerrey'n valley. Ta tom mooar barbrag ec giat y gharey eck. Ta duillagyn beggey er y barbrag, as messyn ruy ayns Mean Fouyir.

Un fastyr, hie Riwal dys y barbrag dy hroggal ny messyn. Ta Soazig jannoo soo jeh messyn y barbrag. Agh ta birragyn geyre er y barbrag, as ren ny birragyn giarey laueyn Riwal. Haink eh stiagh as fuill er e laueyn.

“Ta ny birragyn shoh ro gheyre,” dooyrt eh. “Lhig dooin giarey sheese y barbrag.”

“Cha jean mee shen,” dooyrt Soazig. “Ta faasechredjue ayns y valley shoh: cha lhisagh peiagh erbee giarey y barbrag ec y giat. My nee peiagh erbee giarey eh, hig drogh haghyrt er y thie.”

“Faasechredjue!” dooyrt Riwal. “Cha nel ayn agh tom.”

Ren Soazig gearey, as hug ee eh dy hoie ec yn aile. “Lhig dou skeeal y ghra dhyt,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n skeeal shen y vun jeh'n faasechredjue.”

“Roish ram cheeadyn dy vleeantyn, va filliuyn 'syn ellan. Va filliu mooar liauyr cummal er ny sleityn. Un geurey, va sniaghtey trome ayn, as cha row bee erbee er son y filliu. Haink keoieid er y filliu, son nagh row bee echey. Lesh y keoieid shen, haink eh sheese dys y valley 'syn oie, as ghow eh kirree.

“Va inneen aeg 'sy valley as fys eck er red ennagh druaiaghtagh. Ren ee soiaghey barbrag mygeayrt y valley, as feoghaig fo'n barbrag. Ghow ee arrane druaiaghtagh harrish y barbrag. Tra haink y filliu reesht, ren ny birragyn giarey e chassyn, as cha row eh abyl çheet stiagh. Va ny blaaghyn gorrym feoghaig gial 'syn oie, as va aggle er y filliu roue. Hie yn filliu ersooyl gys ny sleityn, as cha daink eh rieau reesht.”

“As ta'n barbrag shen foast ec y giat?” dooyrt Riwal.

“Ta,” dooyrt Soazig. “Shen y barbrag. As jeeagh fo: ta feoghaig gaase ayn foast, lesh blaaghyn gorrym 'sy tourey.”

Smooinee Riwal tammylt. “Ta'n skeeal aalin,” dooyrt eh, “agh cha nel ayn agh faasechredjue. T'eh gollrish yn astroaylleeaght 'sy phabyr ayd. Ta dty phabyr gra dy chooilley laa cre hig orrin, rere ny rollageyn.”

Ren Soazig gearey ny smoo. “Ta mee lhaih yn astroaylleeaght,” dooyrt ee, “agh cha nel mee credjal ayn. Ta mee credjal ayns skeealyn mie. Agh cha jean mee giarey sheese y barbrag.”

Lurg shen, hug Soazig lheihys er laueyn Riwal, as ren ad yn soo cooidjagh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren ny birragyn er y barbrag?
Ren ny birragyn giarey laueyn Riwal.
Cre'n faasechredjue t'ayns y valley mychione y barbrag?
Cha lhisagh peiagh erbee giarey y barbrag ec y giat, ny hig drogh haghyrt er y thie.
Cre'n fa haink y filliu sheese dys y valley?
Haink keoieid er y filliu, son nagh row bee erbee echey 'sy sniaghtey.
Cre ren yn inneen aeg?
Ren ee soiaghey barbrag as feoghaig mygeayrt y valley, as ghow ee arrane druaiaghtagh harrish y barbrag.
Vel Soazig credjal ayns yn astroaylleeaght?
Cha nel. T'ee lhaih yn astroaylleeaght, agh cha nel ee credjal ayn.

lessons.title: Eirys y naim
lessons.summary: In a letter to his sister Gwladys in England, Hefin Nankivell tells what their paternal uncle left: the house in the village, a small annuity for their mother, an investment in the village wind turbine, his old pipe holder and a heraldic sign over the fire; the lawyer Eimear Prigent verifies the will, and the truth about the sign comes out: the uncle bought it at a market and it is no hereditary sign at all.
lessons.text:
Gwladys veen,

Ta mee screeu hood veih thie nyn naim ayroil 'sy valley. Ta mee soie ec e voayrd, as ta'n thie feer feayr. Ta fys ayd dy row nyn naim ayroil gollrish ayr dooin, lurg baase nyn ayr. Nish ta mee er vakin y screeuyn echey, as ta mee laccal ginsh dhyt mychione yn eirys.

Haink ny screeuyn veih'n leighder, Eimear Prigent. Hie mee dys yn oik eck 'sy voghrey. Ren ee firrinaghey ny screeuyn: ennym nyn naim, ny feanishyn, as y laa. “Ta feme aym er firrinaghey dagh red,” dooyrt ee. “Eisht vees yn eirys aarloo.” Ta'n firrinaghey jeant nish.

Shoh yn eirys. Ta'n thie ain, dhyt's as dou. Ta bleeanaght beg ec nyn moir: argid dagh blein, rish e bea. Cha nel y bleeanaght mooar, agh nee'n bleeanaght cur argid jee son bee as aile 'sy gheurey. Va nyn naim ayroil kinjagh kiarail mychione nyn moir. As va ynesteeaght ec nyn naim ayns turbeen geayee y valley. Ren eh yn ynesteeaght shen roish jeih bleeaney, tra va sleih y valley troggal y turbeen cooidjagh. Ta'n ynesteeaght cur argid beg dooin dy chooilley vlein. Ta mee credjal dy lhisagh shin freayll yn ynesteeaght, son dy row graih echey er y turbeen.

Hooar mee neesht y greimmeyder echey: greimmeyder piob jeh fuygh doo. Ta cooinaghtyn aym er nyn naim soie ec yn aile lesh y greimmeyder ayns e veeal. Cha nel mee jannoo ymmyd jeh piob, agh freayll-ym y greimmeyder.

As nish, y cowrey heraldagh. Ta cooinaghtyn ayd er y cowrey heraldagh erskyn yn aile: scell gorrym as ushag vuigh er. Va nyn naim gra dy row eh eiraghtoil, cowrey nyn lught-thie veih ny shenn laghyn. “Ta'n cowrey shoh eiraghtoil,” v'eh gra rish dy chooilley pheiagh. Va mee credjal eh, as va graih ain er.

Agh hooar mee fys ny firriney 'sy voghrey. Ayns kishtey fo'n lhiabbee, va pabyr beg: lioar-chreck veih margey ayns Sostyn, veih'n vlein 1971. Ren nyn naim kionnaghey'n cowrey heraldagh er three punt! Cha row eh eiraghtoil ec traa erbee. She firriney lhome ee. Ren mee gearey derrey va mee ching.

Ta mee smooinaghtyn dy row fys ec nyn naim er y firriney rish e vea ooilley, as dy row eh gearey neesht. Ta mee er hroggal y cowrey heraldagh reesht erskyn yn aile. Cha nel eh eiraghtoil, agh t'eh ain nish, as nee eh ve eiraghtoil veih shoh magh.

Tar dys y valley cha leah as nee oo. Ta ram dy yannoo 'sy thie.

Lesh graih,
Hefin

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ren firrinaghey ny screeuyn?
Ren y leighder, Eimear Prigent, firrinaghey ny screeuyn.
Cre'n bleeanaght t'ec nyn moir?
Ta bleeanaght beg eck: argid dagh blein rish e bea.
C'raad va ynesteeaght nyn naim?
Va'n ynesteeaght echey ayns turbeen geayee y valley.
Cre hooar Hefin ayns y kishtey fo'n lhiabbee?
Hooar eh lioar-chreck veih margey ayns Sostyn: va'n cowrey heraldagh kionnit er three punt.
Row'n cowrey heraldagh eiraghtoil?
Cha row. Cha row eh eiraghtoil ec traa erbee.

lessons.title: Yn ellynlann 'sy chabbal
lessons.summary: The painter Gwern Ruthven opens a small art gallery in an old chapel in the village: paintings of parallel lines, and a film projected on the wall by an old lamp; the influential critic Mhairi Lennox comes from Douglas and criticises the show as metaphysical, but the villagers show a sensitivity she had not expected, and her review praises Gwern's persistence after all.
lessons.text:
Ta Gwern Ruthven ny ellyneyr. Rish queig bleeaney, t'eh er ve jannoo jallooyn ayns shenn chabbal 'sy valley. Cha row peiagh erbee jannoo ymmyd jeh'n chabbal, as ren Gwern eh y chionnaghey er argid beg. 'Sy vlein shoh, ren eh ellynlann beg jeh. Ayns yn ellynlann, ta jallooyn echey er ny boallaghyn, as ta stoyl ec y dorrys son ny sleih.

Ta jallooyn Gwern feer neuchadjin. Ta linnaghyn colinney ayns dagh jalloo: linnaghyn liauyr, gorrym as glass, colinney rish y cheilley, gollrish ny magheryn as y keayn 'sy valley. “Cha nel ny linnaghyn colinney dy bragh çheet cooidjagh,” ta Gwern gra. “T'ad gollrish daa pheiagh ta cummal 'sy valley cheddin, nagh vel loayrt rish y cheilley.”

Ec jerrey yn ellynlann, ta farhilgane er y voalley. Ta Gwern er ghoaill shenn lampey scannane veih e ayr. Ta'n lampey shen soilshaghey scannane er y voalley: ny tonnyn ec y traie, rish oor. Ta'n farhilgane mooar, as ta'n shamyr dorraghey, as cha nel soilshey erbee agh y lampey.

Haink cremeyder dys yn ellynlann veih Doolish: Mhairi Lennox. She cremeyder feer cummeydagh ee. Ta'n art eck 'sy phabyr-naight dagh shiaghtin, as t'ee yn cremeyder smoo cummeydagh 'syn ellan. Ta sleih goll dys taishbynys tra t'ee gra dy vel eh mie. Ta aggle er ellyneyryn, son dy vel ee cremmey dy geyre.

Ren Mhairi jeeaghyn er ny jallooyn as er y farhilgane rish lieh oor. Eisht dooyrt ee rish Gwern: “Ta ny jallooyn ayd metafissigoil, as cha nel eh shen mie. Linnaghyn colinney, as farhilgane tonnyn: c'raad ta bea y valley?” Va Mhairi cremmey yn taishbynys ooilley.

Agh eisht haink sleih y valley stiagh: eirinee, eeasteyryn, paitçhyn. Hass shenn eeasteyr roish y farhilgane rish oor slane. “Shen y traie raad hooar my ayr baase 'sy cheayn,” dooyrt eh rish Mhairi. Hass ben aeg roish jalloo nyn linnaghyn colinney. “Ta mee as my shuyr gollrish ny linnaghyn shoh,” dooyrt ee. Va ennaghtaght mooar ec sleih y valley son ny jallooyn. Cha row Mhairi er yerkal rish ennaghtaght myr shen.

Ayns y phabyr-naight er y Jesarn ny lurg shen, cha row Mhairi cremmey Gwern myr v'eh er yerkal. “Ta ny jallooyn metafissigoil,” screeu ee, “agh ta kinjid baghtal ayn. Rish queig bleeaney, ta'n ellyneyr shoh er jannoo jalloo dagh laa ayns shenn chabbal gyn argid. Ta kinjid myr shen neuchadjin. As ta ennaghtaght ec sleih y valley nagh vaik mee rieau ayns ellynlann ayns Doolish.”

Lurg yn art shen, haink ram sleih dys yn ellynlann veih Doolish. Ta Gwern foast jannoo ny jallooyn echey, dagh laa.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n boayl ta ellynlann Gwern?
Ta'n ellynlann echey ayns shenn chabbal 'sy valley.
Cre ta ry-akin ayns jallooyn Gwern?
Ta linnaghyn colinney ry-akin ayns dagh jalloo.
Cre ta'n lampey jannoo?
Ta'n lampey soilshaghey scannane jeh ny tonnyn er y voalley.
Cre'n fa ta aggle er ellyneyryn mychione Mhairi Lennox?
She cremeyder feer cummeydagh ee, as t'ee cremmey dy geyre.
Cre dooyrt Mhairi rish Gwern ec y toshiaght?
Dooyrt ee dy vel ny jallooyn echey metafissigoil.
Cre screeu Mhairi mychione Gwern 'sy phabyr-naight?
Screeu ee dy vel kinjid baghtal ayns ny jallooyn echey.

lessons.title: Yn claare coloayrtagh
lessons.summary: After a year's hiatus, Aeron Morvan's radio talk show comes back, and the first subject is a plan to put asphalt on the old lane through the village; the councillor Nolwenn Guivarch speaks with zeal for it, a caller blames globalisation for the big lorries, Aeron stops a man who uses a derogatory word and one who is threatening, and they talk about good manners and the narrowing of the road by the school.
lessons.text:
Ta Aeron Morvan stiureyder claare coloayrtagh er y radio. Dagh Jemayrt, t'eh loayrt mychione cooishyn y valley, as ta sleih çheet er y çhellvane dy ghra nyn smooinaghtyn. Agh rish blein, cha row claare coloayrtagh erbee ayn: va hiatys ayn, son dy row Aeron ching. 'Sy vlein shoh, lurg yn hiatys, haink y claare er-ash.

“Fastyr mie,” dooyrt Aeron. “Ta mee gennal dy vel y hiatys harrish. Jiu, ta shin loayrt mychione y raad.”

Ta raad beg shenn goll trooid y valley, faggys da'n scoill. Ta'n reiltys laccal asfalt noa y chur er y raad, as y raad y yannoo ny smoo lhean. Haink Nolwenn Guivarch, oltey jeh coonseil y valley, dys y claare. Va jeeanid mooar eck son y raad. “Ta ram towlyn ayns y raad ain,” dooyrt ee lesh jeeanid. “Lesh asfalt noa, bee yn raad sauçhey son gleashtanyn as son paitçhyn.” Cha row peiagh erbee er y claare lesh jeeanid wheesh as Nolwenn.

Haink ben veih'n thalloo er y çhellvane hoshiaght. “Cha nel mee laccal asfalt,” dooyrt ee. “She cruinneydaght shoh. Ta cruinneydaght cur gleashtanyn mooarey trooid y valley veih dy chooilley ard jeh'n theihll. Cha nel feme ain er raad ny smoo lhean son gleashtanyn mooarey.”

Haink dooinney er y çhellvane eisht, as va corree mooar er. Dooyrt eh fockle leodagh mychione sleih noa ta çheet dy chummal 'sy valley. Ren Aeron lhiettal eh. “Cha nel mee laccal fockle leodagh myr shen er y claare shoh,” dooyrt Aeron. “Ta beasaght scanshoil. Loayr mychione y raad, as freayll dty veasaght.”

Va'n nah dooinney ny smoo baggyrtagh foast. “My hig yn asfalt,” dooyrt eh, “nee'm ny gleashtanyn y lhiettal lesh carbyd mooar 'sy raad!” Va'n coraa echey baggyrtagh, as hug Aeron jerrey er y çhellvane. “Cha nel feme ain er coraa baggyrtagh,” dooyrt Aeron. “Ta shin abyl loayrt dy meen.”

Er y jerrey, haink shenn ven er y çhellvane. “Ta keylaghey 'sy raad faggys da'n scoill,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n raad giare as keyl ayns shen, as ta'n keylaghey shen cur er ny gleashtanyn goll dy moal. Ta'n keylaghey freayll ny paitçhyn sauçhey. Lhig da'n asfalt çheet, agh freayll-jee yn keylaghey.”

Cha dooyrt Nolwenn veg son tammylt. Eisht dooyrt ee: “Ta shen coyrle vie. Nee'm loayrt rish y coonseil mychione y keylaghey.”

“Shoh jerrey'n claare,” dooyrt Aeron. “Va beasaght vie ec y chooid smoo jiu. Hig y claare coloayrtagh er-ash er Jemayrt ny lurg shen, gyn hiatys!”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va hiatys ayns y claare coloayrtagh?
Va hiatys ayn son dy row Aeron ching rish blein.
Cre ta'n reiltys laccal cur er y raad?
Ta'n reiltys laccal asfalt noa y chur er y raad.
Cre'n fa nagh vel yn chied ven laccal asfalt?
T'ee gra dy vel cruinneydaght cur gleashtanyn mooarey trooid y valley.
Cre ren Aeron tra dooyrt y dooinney fockle leodagh?
Ren Aeron lhiettal eh, as dooyrt eh dy vel beasaght scanshoil.
Cre ta'n keylaghey faggys da'n scoill jannoo?
Ta'n keylaghey cur er ny gleashtanyn goll dy moal, as t'eh freayll ny paitçhyn sauçhey.

lessons.title: Garey Katell
lessons.summary: Katell Rowse, a retired teacher, gets her garden ready for the village show with her companion, an old dog: an asparagus bed, basil in the warm window, garlic cloves in rows and a plant with palm-shaped leaves; the neighbour's boy Fionnlagh finds tadpoles eating each other in her pond, and she explains that cannibalism is common among them, and that the island's mild weather has few extremes.
lessons.text:
Ta Katell Rowse er ve ny ben-ynsee rish daeed blein. Nish, t'ee cummal ayns thie beg ec mullagh y valley, as ta garey mooar eck. T'ee cummal ny lomarcan, agh ta moddey shenn eck, as she yn moddey y cooidjaghtagh eck. T'eh shooyl marish dy chooilley voayl. “Ta moddey yn cooidjaghtagh share,” t'ee gra. “Cha nel eh rieau loayrt ro liauyr.”

Ec jerrey'n tourey, bee taishbynys garaghyn 'sy valley. Ta Katell laccal yn chied ynnyd y chosney. T'ee gobbraghey 'sy gharey dagh laa, as ta'n moddey lhie 'sy ghrian faggys jee.

Ta asparag ec Katell 'sy gharey. Ta'n asparag goaill traa liauyr: ren ee soiaghey yn asparag roish three bleeaney, as cha nel ee giarey eh agh nish. Dagh moghrey ayns Boaldyn, t'ee giarey yn asparag noa, glass as çheh veih'n ghrian. Ta blass feer vie er asparag noa.

Ayns uinnag y thie, ta bassyl gaase ayns kishtey beg. Ta'n bassyl laccal çhiass as grian, as cha nel ee gaase mie 'sy gharey. Ta Katell cur bassyl ayns bee Iddaalagh, as ta blass bassyl ayns y thie ooilley.

Ayns linney liauyr, ta ingaghyn soit eck. Ta dagh cruinnag garleid rheynnit ayns ingaghyn. Ayns Mean Fouyir, ta Katell soiaghey dagh ingey ny lomarcan 'sy thalloo, as 'sy tourey, ta dagh ingey er jannoo cruinnag noa. Ta lus elley eck ec y voalley, lesh duillagyn bassagh: ta dagh duillag gollrish laue, lesh queig meir. “Ta ny duillagyn bassagh shoh aalin,” t'ee gra. “Cha nel lus erbee elley lesh duillagyn bassagh 'sy valley.”

Un laa, haink Fionnlagh, guilley y naboo, harrish y voalley. V'eh shey bleeaney d'eash. Ren eh jeeaghyn ayns y logh beg 'sy gharey. Va ram rannagyn aegey 'syn ushtey. “Jeeagh!” dooyrt eh. “Ta ny rannagyn beggey gee y cheilley!”

“She cannablaght t'ayn,” dooyrt Katell. “Ta cannablaght cadjin mastey rannagyn aegey. Tra nagh vel bee dy liooar ayns y logh, ta ny rannagyn mooarey gee ny rannagyn beggey. T'eh feer hrome, agh ta cannablaght ny ayrn jeh dooghys.”

Cha row Fionnlagh feer ghennal lesh y cannablaght. “Vel ny rannagyn gee y cheilley 'sy gheurey neesht?” dooyrt eh.

“Cha nel ram,” dooyrt Katell. “Cha nel feeganyn mooarey 'syn emshir ain. Cha nel y geurey ro feayr, as cha nel y tourey ro çheh. Ta sniaghtey trome neuchadjin ayns Ellan Vannin, as cha nel feegan erbee ayns y çhiass. Er-y-fa shen, ta'n garey gaase mie, as ta'n logh slane.”

Ec y taishbynys, hooar Katell yn nah ynnyd son yn asparag eck. Cha dooar y moddey ynnyd erbee, agh hooar eh bee mie lurg y taishbynys.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi yn cooidjaghtagh ec Katell?
She yn moddey shenn eck y cooidjaghtagh eck.
Cre'n fa ta bassyl gaase 'syn uinnag?
Ta'n bassyl laccal çhiass as grian.
Cre ta Katell soiaghey 'sy thalloo?
T'ee soiaghey dagh ingey ny lomarcan 'sy thalloo.
Cre honnick Fionnlagh 'sy logh?
Honnick eh rannagyn aegey gee y cheilley: cannablaght.
Vel feeganyn mooarey 'syn emshir ayns Ellan Vannin?
Cha nel. Cha nel y geurey ro feayr, as cha nel y tourey ro çheh.

lessons.title: Possan kiaullee ayns ny barrickyn
lessons.summary: The village band, led by the clarinettist Erwan Trevaskis, practises in the old barracks of a wartime airfield; an electrician explains the old alternating-current wiring and puts in an ionisation smoke alarm, the band cleans the rust off an old plane's undercarriage to keep as a memorial, and the old airman Torcuil Macphail, who thought he saw soldiers in the barracks at night, learns from his doctor that his new medicine gave him hallucinations.
lessons.text:
Ec jerrey'n valley, ta shenn ynnyd etlanyn veih'n Nah Chaggey Mooar. Ta ny shenn barrickyn foast ayns shen: thieyn liauyr injil, raad va deiney aegey yn armee cadley 'sy chaggey. Nish, ta thie y valley ayns y thie smoo jeh ny barrickyn. Dagh Jerdein, ta possan kiaullee y valley cliaghtey ayns shen.

She Erwan Trevaskis stiureyder y phossan. T'eh cloie y clarinaid. Ta three clarinaidyn 'sy phossan, as daa feddan, as drummyn. Ta Erwan gra dy vel y clarinaid yn greie share 'sy theihll. “Ta'n clarinaid abyl gra dagh red,” t'eh gra, “red trimshagh as red gennal.”

Ta ny barrickyn shenn, as ta'n lectraghys shenn neesht. Haink fer-lectraghys dy yeeaghyn er. “Ta stroo kirkinagh 'sy thie,” dooyrt eh rish Erwan. “Ta dy chooilley thie ayns Ellan Vannin goaill stroo kirkinagh, agh ta ny snaieyn lectragh shoh feer shenn.” Hug eh snaieyn noa ayns ny boallaghyn. Hug eh greie raaue jaagh er y mullagh neesht. “Ta'n greie shoh gobbraghey lesh eeaneaghey,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n eeaneaghey cur enney er jaagh beg, roish my vees aile ayn.” Cha row Erwan toiggal yn eeaneaghey dy slane, agh va'n greie shickyr.

Cooyl ny barrickyn, ayns y faiyr, va red mooar jeh yiarn: focharriads shenn etlan. Va'n etlan er duittym ec yn ynnyd 'sy chaggey, as va'n focharriads faagit ayns shen. Va merg trome er: va'n yiarn ruy as ouyr lesh merg. Ren y possan kiaullee yn merg y ghlenney, laa er laa, lurg ny cliaghtaghyn. Nish ta'n focharriads glen, gyn merg, ec dorrys thie y valley, myr cooinaghtyn er deiney yn armee.

Ta Torcuil Macphail kiare bleeaney as kiare feed d'eash. V'eh ny ghooinney aeg 'syn armee ayns ny barrickyn shoh 'sy chaggey. Ta Torcuil cloie ny drummyn 'sy phossan. Un Jerdein, dooyrt eh rish Erwan: “Ta mee er vakin deiney aegey ayns ny barrickyn 'syn oie, ayns eaddagh caggee, as ad soie ec y boayrd.”

Va aggle er Erwan son y shenn dooinney. Hie Torcuil dys y lhee. Ren y lhee briaght jeh mychione y lheihys echey. Va lheihys noa er ve currit da roish shiaghtin. “Ta branlaadee reayrtagh çheet ass y lheihys shoh ny keayrtyn,” dooyrt y lhee. “Va branlaadagh ayd. Cha row deiney erbee ayns ny barrickyn.” Hug y lhee lheihys elley da, as cha daink branlaadagh erbee reesht.

Er y Jerdein ny lurg shen, ghow Torcuil ny drummyn echey reesht. “Cha nel ny deiney aegey ayns ny barrickyn,” dooyrt eh, “agh ta mee foast cooinaghtyn orroo.” Ren y possan kiaullee cloie arrane shenn veih'n chaggey, as ren Erwan cloie y clarinaid er e hon.

Feyshtyn:
Cre t'ayns ny shenn barrickyn nish?
Ta thie y valley ayns ny barrickyn, as ta'n possan kiaullee cliaghtey ayns shen.
Cre'n stroo lectragh t'ayns y thie?
Ta stroo kirkinagh ayn.
Cre'n greie ta Erwan cloie?
T'eh cloie y clarinaid.
Cre hug y fer-lectraghys er y mullagh?
Hug eh greie raaue jaagh er y mullagh, ta gobbraghey lesh eeaneaghey.
Cre ren y possan lesh y focharriads?
Ren ad yn merg y ghlenney jeh'n focharriads.
Cre'n fa honnick Torcuil deiney aegey 'syn oie?
Va branlaadagh echey, er-y-fa'n lheihys noa.
